topic: How the 1970s oil crisis sparked stagflation in the US

script.title: 1970s oil shock sparked America’s stagflation – why it mattered
script.hook: Did the oil shock really create America’s first stagflation?

scenes.text: Did the oil shock really create America’s first stagflation?
Oil prices jumped about threefold in 1973, ending cheap energy.
Gasoline rose to roughly one thirty dollars per gallon.
Businesses faced higher production costs and could not raise wages.

motion_action.statement: Higher costs and stagnant wages drove a squeeze

scenes.text: Result: GDP growth stalled while inflation surged past ten percent.
The Fed raised interest rates to fifteen percent, choking credit.
Unemployment climbed to six percent, a rare double‑whammy.
Economists call this mix stagflation – stagnant growth plus inflation.
It persisted through the late seventies, only easing after 1980 policy shifts.
So the oil shock’s legacy is clear:
